commentary:
1. SCORE & MOMENTUM
The Chicago Bulls have dismantled the Milwaukee defense, heading into the locker room with a commanding 62-39 lead. Chicago’s offensive efficiency is staggering, evidenced by a 0.558 eFG% and a 0.455 clip from beyond the arc. Milwaukee’s momentum is in a deep hole at -5, exacerbated by a disastrous 17 turnovers that have fueled the Bulls' transition game.

2. KEY PLAYER ANALYSIS
Jalen Smith has paced the Bulls with 11 points, providing a steady hand to maintain Chicago's double-digit cushion. Cormac Ryan is doing his best to keep Milwaukee afloat with 10 points, but he lacks support as the Bucks' starters have failed to record a single assist. With Milwaukee shooting a dismal 0.302 from the floor, Ryan needs a historic second half to bridge this massive gap.

3. X-FACTORS / FOUL TROUBLE
Milwaukee’s inability to protect the ball is the primary driver of this blowout, as their 0.59 AST/TO ratio is being dwarfed by Chicago’s 1.55. While the Bucks are winning the battle on the glass with a 0.393 OREB% and a +3 rebound differential, these second-chance opportunities are being squandered by poor shooting. Both teams are managing foul trouble, with one starter on each side already sitting at three personal fouls.

4. SECOND-HALF OUTLOOK
The Bulls are firmly in control and will secure a 17-point victory when the final buzzer sounds. Milwaukee’s 0.200 shooting from three-point range offers no path to a comeback against a Chicago squad that is capitalizing on every mistake. Expect Chicago to maintain their high-percentage shot selection and cruise to a comfortable win.
